params.question: Why does iron deficiency anaemia develop more readily during pregnancy despite normal dietary intake?

answers.text: Pregnancy increases urinary iron excretion beyond 5 mg per day

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The body has no regulated pathway for excreting iron through the kidneys. Iron is lost only through blood loss, menstruation, and desquamation of cells.

answers.text: The placenta actively blocks iron absorption from the duodenum

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The placenta does not interfere with duodenal absorption. In fact, pregnancy hormones may upregulate iron absorption, but this increase is insufficient to meet the sharply rising demand.

answers.text: Increased iron demand exceeds the gut's limited absorptive capacity of 1–2 mg per day

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The body recycles 25 mg of iron daily but can absorb only 1–2 mg from food. In pregnancy, the growing foetus, expanding blood volume, and placenta raise demand well beyond this narrow absorptive capacity.

answers.text: Pregnancy suppresses transferrin production by the liver

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Transferrin production actually increases during pregnancy to meet higher transport demand. Low transferrin would lower TIBC, but in iron deficiency TIBC is characteristically elevated.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the iron balance concept: daily recycling provides 25 mg, but absorption adds only 1–2 mg. When demand exceeds this narrow absorptive capacity — as in pregnancy — stores deplete and deficiency develops.
Exactly. The gut can absorb only 1–2 mg/day, while the body recycles ~25 mg internally. Pregnancy sharply raises demand beyond what absorption alone can cover, depleting stores.

interactions.label: A patient is advised to take oral iron tablets with orange juice and avoid tea.

params.question: A patient is advised to take oral iron tablets with orange juice and avoid tea. Which mechanism best explains this dietary advice?

answers.text: Orange juice raises gastric pH, improving iron solubility in the alkaline environment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Orange juice is acidic, not alkaline. A low-pH environment actually helps iron absorption by keeping iron in its reduced, absorbable ferrous form.

answers.text: Vitamin C enhances iron absorption while polyphenols in tea inhibit it

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) promotes reduction of ferric iron to ferrous iron, facilitating uptake via DMT1. Polyphenols in tea chelate iron in the gut lumen, preventing absorption.

answers.text: Tea contains excess calcium that competes with iron for binding to DMT1

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While calcium does inhibit iron absorption, tea's primary inhibitory compounds are polyphenols (tannins), not calcium. Dairy products are the main dietary source of calcium-mediated inhibition.

answers.text: Vitamin C converts ferric iron directly to haem iron for faster absorption

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Vitamin C reduces ferric (Fe³⁺) to ferrous (Fe²⁺) iron, facilitating non-haem iron absorption via DMT1. It does not convert inorganic iron into haem iron — haem iron comes only from animal haemoglobin and myoglobin.

overallFeedback.feedback: Recall the enhancers and inhibitors discussed: vitamin C and gastric acid promote absorption by maintaining iron in its ferrous form, while polyphenols (tea, coffee), phytates (cereals), and calcium reduce it.

Correct. Vitamin C and gastric acid both enhance non-haem iron absorption, while polyphenols, phytates, and calcium inhibit it. This is why iron supplements are best taken before food with a source of vitamin C.

interactions.label: In iron deficiency, serum ferritin falls only after haemoglobin begins to declin

params.question: In iron deficiency, serum ferritin falls only after haemoglobin begins to decline.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Ferritin is actually the earliest marker to fall, not the last. The body depletes storage iron first — ferritin drops while serum iron, TIBC, and haemoglobin remain normal. Only after stores are exhausted does transport iron decline, and haemoglobin falls last.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — ferritin reflects storage iron, which is the first pool the body draws upon. Serum ferritin falls while serum iron, TIBC, and haemoglobin are all still normal, making it the earliest and most sensitive marker of iron deficiency.

metadata.title: In iron deficiency, serum ferritin falls

interactions.label: A patient has low serum iron, elevated TIBC, and transferrin saturation below 15

params.question: A patient has low serum iron, elevated TIBC, and transferrin saturation below 15%, but haemoglobin is still within the normal range. Which stage of iron deficiency does this represent?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: In stage 1, only ferritin is low. Serum iron, TIBC, and haemoglobin are all normal. The abnormalities described here — low serum iron, high TIBC, low transferrin saturation — indicate that transport iron has also been affected.

In stage 2, storage iron is exhausted and transport iron begins to fail. Serum iron drops, TIBC rises (the liver produces more transferrin to scavenge iron), and transferrin saturation falls below 15%. Haemoglobin is still maintained.
Stage 3 is defined by frank anaemia — haemoglobin falls, MCV drops below 80 fL, and the peripheral smear shows microcytic hypochromic red cells. This patient's haemoglobin is still normal.

In anaemia of chronic disease, serum iron is low but TIBC is typically low or normal (not elevated), and ferritin is raised due to inflammation-driven hepcidin excess. The elevated TIBC here points to iron deficiency, not chronic disease.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the sequence: ferritin falls first (stage 1), then transport markers change — serum iron drops, TIBC rises, transferrin saturation falls below 15% (stage 2) — and only lastly does haemoglobin drop (stage 3).

Exactly. The pattern of low serum iron, high TIBC, and low transferrin saturation with a normal haemoglobin defines stage 2 — iron-deficient erythropoiesis, where the marrow is starving but hasn't yet failed.
